newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc falls to 14-month low against mark.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc falls to 14-month low against mark.

text.p: 1515 GMT - The Swiss franc tumbled to a 14-month low against the mark as retail customer continued to liquidate their short mark/swiss positions built up earlier this year on the expectation the mark is on the rise, dealers said.
Dealers expect the trend to continue in the medium-term and see the mark possibly rising to 83.50 or even 84 Swiss centimes by the end of the year. Initial resistance is seen at 82.95.
Trading volumes, however, remain rather thin and the mark strengthening could also be slightly excessive.
The change in sentiment was triggered by Wednesday's comments by Bundesbank's chief economist Otmar Issing that there was no need to lower key rates further.
In addition, markets are also becoming convinced of the Swiss National Bank's commitment toward keeping Swiss rates low.
Part of the pressure on the franc is also coming from sales of Swiss francs against French francs and yen, dealers added.
On Thursday the franc slipped below its July level and has now hit a year low and is at levels not seen since August 1995.

The franc's rise in 1995 was connected with inflows by German investors that were unnerved over Europe's single currency, the euro, slated to begin in 1999. * Mark ends at 82.90/93 centimes vs 82.69/70 this morning and Thursday's closer at 82.57/59. It easily overcame resistance at 82.75, dealer said. It ended near the day's high of 82.91. * Dollar ends at 1.2625/2635 francs vs its 1.2580/2590 opener. * Benchmark 3-month Eurofrancs at 1.53/1.78 percent vs last night's 1.46/1.71 percent.
